title: ACP interface v1
description: ACP's own published, versioned, cross-protocol interface: the single owner of background/synchronous compression state (acp.coordinator.Coordinator), exposed over authenticated loopback HTTP for a host adapter (e.g. a future Phase-4 Claude/Codex adapter) or a local test harness to depend on, without importing an acp.* Python module, instantiating Coordinator directly, or reading '.acp/' private on-disk state beyond the two bootstrap files this document carves out. Per agent_protocols_v1_background_compression_adjustment_metadata_v1.md §17, no host adapter is permitted to run its own compression operation or manipulate '.acp/' private files directly -- every operation below is the only sanctioned path to ACP's coordinator.

excluded_from_this_interface.coordinator.internal_state: Job dict internals, cache keys/entries, and lock state are never exposed in any form. service.status is a bounded, aggregated view only (job counts by state, AALP reachability, a pressure-mode snapshot) -- see its response schema below.
excluded_from_this_interface.raw_source.read: source.store registers raw authoritative content addressed by its hash for provenance/audit purposes only. There is no operation in this interface to read stored raw bytes back out; a host adapter that needs the original payload again must already hold it (ACP never becomes the system of record for retrieving raw source).
excluded_from_this_interface.provider_credential.any: ACP never holds or exposes an AALP provider credential in any form -- credentials remain AALP-owned administrative functionality, entirely outside ACP's own interface (see agent-api-lane-protocol/interface/v1/contract.json's own exclusion of credential.read/write/probe).

authentication.mechanism: single bearer secret over a loopback HTTP connection
authentication.notes: ACP has exactly one class of authorized local client: a host adapter process on the same machine (a future Phase-4 deliverable) or a local test harness. The bearer secret is transport/session bootstrap material, not a per-request credential, and is out of scope for this document's field-level schemas. It is never a provider credential, and this interface never exposes a provider credential in any form (see excluded_from_this_interface).

bootstrap.summary: How a client discovers where ACP is listening and what bearer secret to send, without reading any other ACP-private on-disk state.

descriptor_file.acp_root_resolution: ACP_HOME environment variable if set, else the current working directory ACP was started from (acp.containment.resolve_root -- the same resolution convention used by every other '.acp/' consumer in this repository). A client must be told this root out-of-band (e.g. via shared deployment configuration); interface v1 defines no discovery operation for locating an unknown root.

format.secret_file: string, absolute path to the bearer secret file

descriptor_file.written: atomically, by ACP's ingress on startup, before it begins accepting connections

secret_file.format: opaque bearer token, raw bytes, no trailing newline guaranteed
secret_file.permissions: 0600, owner-only, generated once by ACP and never transmitted except as the value clients send back in the Authorization header
secret_file.usage: sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <contents>' on every operation below

bootstrap.carve_out_rationale: Mirrors agent-api-lane-protocol/interface/v1/contract.json's own carve-out for AALP's ingress.json/ingress.secret, applied here to ACP's own ingress: these two files exist specifically so a host adapter can bootstrap a connection to ACP without a hardcoded port or a pre-shared secret out-of-band. They are the one deliberate, narrow exception to 'never read another protocol's -- or, here, ACP's own -- private state from outside its published interface'. Everything else under '.acp/' (raw stored source, job/cache internals, logs) remains off-limits.

transport_binding.notes: Every operation below is this interface's own concrete, normative wire binding -- there is no separate private implementation to reconcile against, unlike AALP's request.forward (which formalizes an already-implemented protocol). A conforming ACP service and a conforming fake service used for host-adapter client tests must both implement this binding exactly as described.
transport_binding.reserved_path_prefix_rule: Every operation is reached under /v1/...; there is no passthrough-style provider-id path segment the way AALP's request.forward uses /{provider_id}/..., so there is no path-prefix collision concern to reserve against here.

outcomes.description: The closed set of outcomes context.evaluate and context.resolve may report, reusing acp.errors.Outcome verbatim (ACP's own outcome set -- ACP never imports AALP's). No cross-protocol client should ever need to handle a value outside this set for these two operations, and no future v1.x addition may repurpose one of these values to mean something else.

success.meaning: The payload was gated and, if inspected, a compressor round-trip through AALP completed and parsed successfully (mode PASS, COMPACT, or COMPRESS -- see the 'mode' response field). A gate BYPASS (payload small enough to skip the compressor entirely) is also reported as 'success' with mode 'PASS'.
success.response_status_code: 200 (context.evaluate/context.resolve); 202 (context.prepare, which reports only a job_id, never an outcome directly)

unavailable.meaning: AALP itself is unreachable or reported its target provider unavailable. No compressed output was produced; the response's 'mode'/'output' fields reflect ACP's own failure policy (passthrough of the original payload, or a placeholder if the payload's failure policy is BLOCK -- see acp.compressor.FailurePolicy).

queue_timeout.meaning: AALP's own admission queue-timeout budget elapsed before the compression request was admitted. Same failure-policy handling as 'unavailable'.

compression_timeout.meaning: A connection-level timeout occurred once an upstream compression attempt started. Same failure-policy handling as 'unavailable'.

total_timeout.meaning: The overall (queue + upstream) timeout budget for the compression round-trip elapsed. Same failure-policy handling as 'unavailable'.

invalid_response.meaning: AALP's response could not be parsed as ACP's own compressor response protocol (missing/invalid ACP-MODE line, unparseable Messages-shaped body). Same failure-policy handling as 'unavailable'.

upstream_error.meaning: AALP itself reported an upstream transport-level failure while forwarding to the provider. Same failure-policy handling as 'unavailable'.

context.evaluate.summary: SYNCHRONOUS GATE (agent_protocols_v1_background_compression_adjustment_metadata_v1.md §11): evaluate/gate one payload synchronously, coalescing with any in-flight job for the same content, and block until a result is available or synchronous_timeout elapses.

flow_id.description: Optional audit/grouping label, forwarded to AALP's own X-Aalp-Flow-Id if a compressor call is made.

synchronous_timeout.description: Seconds to wait on a coalesced in-flight job before falling through to this call's own attempt. Defaults to the coordinator's own configured default when null/absent.

force_policy.description: Overrides the coordinator's own token-count-based failure policy for this call only.

headers.X-Acp-Outcome: the outcome value, e.g. 'compression_timeout' -- REQUIRED, see x_acp_outcome_header below

x_acp_outcome_header.rationale: Mirrors agent-api-lane-protocol/interface/v1/contract.json's request.forward.response.x_aalp_outcome_header requirement exactly: status code alone cannot always unambiguously identify which outcome produced a given response (multiple outcomes share status code 504 or 502), so X-Acp-Outcome must be present on every context.evaluate and context.resolve response, success or not.

context.prepare.summary: BACKGROUND PREFETCH / PRESSURE MAINTENANCE (§11): enqueue/deduplicate background preparation of a payload without blocking the caller. Never installs a result anywhere by itself -- a caller must explicitly context.resolve at its own safe boundary (§12).

request.notes: No synchronous_timeout or force_policy field -- both are context.evaluate-only. A prepared job that fails still resolves to a terminal CompressionResult (never blocks context.resolve indefinitely); force_policy only ever applies to a synchronous evaluate call's own attempt.

possible_outcomes.note: This operation itself never reports a compression Outcome -- only a 202 with a job_id, or a 400 for a malformed request. Its eventual result surfaces later through context.resolve.

context.resolve.summary: Resolve a job previously created by context.prepare (or, less commonly, one context.evaluate itself registered) at a caller's own safe boundary (§12 -- this interface has no opinion on what a safe boundary is).

pending.meaning: The job exists but has not yet reached a terminal state (still QUEUED or RUNNING). This is NOT an error case.

terminal.meaning: The job reached a terminal state with a stored result (READY, or one of the non-timeout/non-success failure states -- see acp.jobs.JobState). Same envelope and X-Acp-Outcome requirement as context.evaluate's response.

unknown_job_id.meaning: The job_id is unknown (never existed, or was already reclaimed by the coordinator's own stale-job sweep). Treated identically to 'pending' -- interface v1 does not distinguish 'never existed' from 'still in flight' at this operation, since a caller has no actionable difference in response to either.

context.pressure.summary: Report/update one receiver's observed context-pressure ratio (§22-23) and get back its current PressureMode.

possible_outcomes.note: Not modeled with the compression Outcome enum -- plain 200/400, mirroring provider.status's own not-outcome-modeled precedent in AALP's contract.

source.store.summary: Register raw authoritative source content, content-addressed by its hash, for provenance/audit purposes.

body.description: Raw content, unmodified. This is the one operation in this interface whose body is the raw payload itself, not a JSON envelope.

source_hash.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 digest of the stored content (acp.provenance.compute_hash).

possible_outcomes.note: Not modeled with the compression Outcome enum -- always 201 on a reachable, authenticated call. Identical content hash-dedupes for free (a repeat store of the same bytes is a no-op write, same returned source_hash).

service.capabilities.summary: Discover ACP's interface version and capability set.

capabilities.description: See top-level 'capabilities'. Absence of a capability string means a client must not assume that behavior is supported.

possible_outcomes.note: Not modeled with the compression Outcome enum. A reachable ACP service always returns 200 with the body above; only a transport-level failure to reach the service at all is possible, and is not an ACP-level outcome.

service.status.summary: Bounded health/status without raw payload or credential exposure -- directly acp.coordinator.Coordinator.status()'s own return value.

jobs_by_state.description: Job counts keyed by acp.jobs.JobState value.

pressure.description: Per-receiver PressureMode name snapshot, keyed by a bounded receiver-key string -- never the raw receiver tuple's own free-form fields beyond host/session_id/agent_id already imply.

explicitly_excluded_fields: any raw payload or compressed output
any AALP bearer secret or other credential
job internals beyond a per-state count (no per-job detail is exposed)

possible_outcomes.note: Not modeled with the compression Outcome enum. Always 200 on a reachable, authenticated call.

receiver.description: Serializes acp.pressure.ReceiverKey, tuple[host, session_id, agent_id-or-None], as an object.

message.description: Non-normative diagnostic text; a client must key behavior off 'outcome', never off this string.

compression_result_envelope.description: Serializes acp.compressor.CompressionResult verbatim. Used identically by context.evaluate's response and context.resolve's terminal response.

compatibility.versioning: Interface major versions are protocol-local to ACP; they need not match AALP's or ADP's interface version numbers.
stays_within_current_major_version_when_: existing outcomes retain their documented meaning
existing clients keep working without adopting any new capability
new fields are optional and/or gated behind a new capability string
service.capabilities exposes any newly added capability
requires_a_new_major_version_when_any_of: an operation or field is removed or renamed
an existing operation's or outcome's semantics change incompatibly
a previously valid request becomes invalid
